newsitem.title: CHILE: RTRS-Chile raises 2000 copper output forecast to 4.7 mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Chile raises 2000 copper output forecast to 4.7 mln tonnes.

text.p: Chile has hiked its copper production forecast to 4.7 million tonnes in 2000 compared with earlier estimates of 3.8 million tonnes due to a rash of new mines and expansion projects, said a state copper board.

The Comision Chilena del Cobre (Cochilco) said its latest estimate has taken into account new pits Los Pelambres and Collahuasi as well as the recently announced oxide heap-leaching operation at the huge Escondida mine.
"The figure could be even be slightly higher as it only includes projects which Cochilco has been officially informed about," Aldo Picozzi, Cochilco's market studies manager, told Reuters.

Projects which have not been taken into account include a possible 150,000 tonne expansion at state-owned copper company Codelco's El Teniente pit and plans to extend Rio Algom's Cerro Colorado mine, he said.
Cochilco estimated in 1995 that copper output would rise to 3.8 million tonnes by the end of the decade. It raised this forecast to nearly 4.3 million tonnes earlier this year.
The studies center expects copper output from Chile -- the world's largest copper producer -- to total 2.5 million tonnes this year, rising to three million tonnes next year and 3.5 million in 1997.
Although there will be an oversupply of copper at the turn of the century, Chile is confident rising demand will prevent copper prices from sagging too far, he said.
"We are not worried. All these new projects are coming on line so the price outlook can't be bad," said Picozzi.
"We assume that rising demand will absorb most of the new production."
